title: Motovun Crowds by Month: When to Avoid Them 2027
metaDescription: Month-by-month crowd levels in Motovun, Croatia, plus the quietest times to visit, truffle-season peaks, parking tips and how to beat the day-trippers.
content:
## Motovun Crowd Levels by Month

Motovun is a walled hilltop town of roughly 500 residents on a 277 m hill above the Mirna valley. Its size is the reason crowds feel heavy: the old town is pedestrianised, there are few streets, and a few hundred day-trippers fill the main square. Crowd levels follow three drivers: truffle season, summer coastal traffic from Istria's beach resorts, and weekends.

### January to March: Quietest Period

These are the emptiest months. Visitors are mostly couples and a few truffle-hunting groups, since black truffle season runs from November to March. Some restaurants and shops shorten their hours or close on weekdays, so check before driving up. Parking is free outside the summer season.

### April and May: Low to Moderate

Visitor numbers rise slowly. Weekdays stay calm and the square is rarely full. Weekends bring tour groups, but they concentrate between 11:00 and 15:00. This is the best balance of open venues and thin crowds.

### June to August: Busy Weekends, Manageable Weekdays

Traffic from the coast pushes weekend numbers up, and parking is paid from roughly June to September. The Motovun Film Festival used to dominate late July, with estimates of up to 21,000 visitors. The 28th edition (21–26 July 2026) was held as Cinehill in Gorski kotar, so the town is no longer guaranteed a festival surge. Confirm the 2027 venue before booking, because a return would triple parking demand and fill rooms inside the walls months ahead.

### September: Moderate, Rising

The summer crowd thins early in the month. Truffle weekends begin to fill the lower car park by mid-morning, so a weekday visit is the safer choice.

### October and November: Peak Season

The White Truffle Days fair runs for seven weekends from early October to mid-November in Livade, just below Motovun. Admission is free, which adds to the numbers. The Teran and Truffle Festival (18–19 October in 2026, about 3,000 visitors, tickets €10–€25) adds a further surge. White truffle season peaks in November, so restaurant tables need booking days ahead.

Most travelers assume the Film Festival is Motovun's real peak. Truffle weekends in October are now the more reliable crowd problem, and weekdays in the same month are far quieter.

### December: Quiet Again

White truffle season continues to the end of December, but the fair weekends are over. Crowds fall sharply after mid-November, and restaurants still serve truffle menus.

## How to Avoid the Crowds in Motovun

- **Pick weekdays.** Tuesday to Thursday is consistently calmer than Saturday and Sunday in every month.
- **Time the day.** Tour groups cluster from 11:00 to 15:00. Arrive before 10:00 or after 17:00 and walk the ramparts with few people around.
- **Park early.** The only visitor car park is at the base, about 400 m below the old town. There is no parking inside the walls. On truffle weekends it fills by mid-morning.
- **Book a dawn truffle hunt.** Early hunts use small groups, with one operator capping at six people. Book ahead, since tours do not always take walk-ins.
- **Skip the fair, keep the truffles.** Eat truffle dishes in a restaurant on a weekday in late November or December instead of the October weekends.
- **Stay overnight.** Evenings, after day-trippers leave, are the emptiest part of any month. Accommodation inside the walls is limited, so book early for summer and October.

## Best Months to Skip the Crowds

For the fewest people, choose January to March or early December. For open venues with light crowds, choose April, May or the first half of September on a weekday. Avoid October and November weekends and peak summer Saturdays.

faq.question: What is the busiest month in Motovun?
faq.answer: October is the busiest month, with November close behind. The White Truffle Days fair runs for seven weekends from early October to mid-November, and the lower car park fills by mid-morning on weekends. Summer Saturdays are the next busiest.

faq.question: When is Motovun least crowded?
faq.answer: January, February and March are the quietest months, followed by December after the truffle fair weekends. Expect few visitors, free parking and shorter opening hours at some restaurants and shops.

faq.question: Is Motovun crowded during the film festival?
faq.answer: Historically yes, with estimates of up to 21,000 visitors in late July. The 2026 edition (21–26 July) moved to Gorski kotar as Cinehill, so check where the 2027 edition will be held. If it returns to Motovun, book accommodation months ahead.

faq.question: What time of day is Motovun quietest?
faq.answer: Before 10:00 and after 17:00 are the quietest hours. Day-trip groups cluster between about 11:00 and 15:00. Staying overnight gives the calmest evenings and mornings.

quickAnswer: Motovun is busiest in October and November during white truffle season, and on summer weekends from June to August. The quietest months are January, February, March and early December. April, May and early September are moderate. Arriving before 10:00 or after 17:00 avoids day-trip coaches in any month.
